tools.name: hw_ila_set_trigger
tools.summary: Set trigger condition on an ILA probe.
tools.description:
Set trigger condition on an ILA probe.

        Supports hex, binary (with don't-care X bits), and decimal values.
        Use hw_ila_set_trigger_condition() to set AND/OR logic between
        multiple probe triggers. Use hw_ila_get_status() to verify setup.

        Args:
            probe: Probe name (e.g. "counter[7:0]" or full path from hw_ila_get_status)
            value: Trigger value. Format depends on radix:
                hex: "FF", "0xFF", "1A2B"
                bin: "11110000", "XXXX1111" (X = don't care, matches any bit)
                     Underscores allowed for readability: "1111_0000"
                dec: "255", "1024" (converted to hex internally)
            operator: Compare operator:
                "eq"  - equal (default)
                "neq" - not equal
                "gt"  - greater than (unsigned)
                "lt"  - less than (unsigned)
            radix: Value format - "hex" (default), "bin", "dec"
            ila: ILA core name (leave empty to auto-select first)

        Examples:
            # Trigger when counter equals 0xFF
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="counter[7:0]", value="FF")

            # Trigger when state machine is NOT in state 3
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="state[1:0]", value="3", operator="neq", radix="dec")

            # Trigger when upper nibble is 0xA, lower nibble is don't-care
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="data[7:0]", value="1010XXXX", radix="bin")

            # Trigger when bit 3 is high, all other bits don't care
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="flags[7:0]", value="XXXX1XXX", radix="bin")

            # Trigger when enable is non-zero (any bit set)
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="enable[3:0]", value="0000", operator="neq", radix="bin")

            # Trigger when address >= 0x1000
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="addr[15:0]", value="1000", operator="gt")

        Returns:
            Confirmation with the applied compare value

tools.name: hw_ila_set_trigger_condition
tools.summary: Set how multiple probe trigger conditions are combined.
tools.description:
Set how multiple probe trigger conditions are combined.

        When multiple probes have trigger values set via hw_ila_set_trigger(),
        this controls whether ALL conditions must match (AND) or ANY single
        condition is enough to trigger (OR).

        Default is AND (all conditions must be true simultaneously).

        Args:
            condition: "AND" (all probes must match) or "OR" (any probe match triggers)
            ila: ILA core name (leave empty to auto-select first)

        Examples:
            # Trigger only when BOTH state==IDLE AND enable==1
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="state[1:0]", value="00", radix="bin")
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="enable", value="1", radix="bin")
            hw_ila_set_trigger_condition(condition="AND")

            # Trigger when EITHER error OR overflow is high
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="error", value="1", radix="bin")
            hw_ila_set_trigger(probe="overflow", value="1", radix="bin")
            hw_ila_set_trigger_condition(condition="OR")

        Returns:
            Confirmation of the trigger condition mode

tools.name: set_bus_skew
tools.summary: Set bus skew constraint (control maximum timing deviation between bus signals)
tools.description:
Set bus skew constraint (control maximum timing deviation between bus signals)

Used to ensure all signals in a parallel bus arrive simultaneously, common for:
- Gray code pointer synchronization in CDC
- Source-synchronous interfaces (DDR, LVDS data buses)
- Multi-bit signal alignment requirements

Args:
    skew_ns: Maximum allowed skew (nanoseconds), recommend setting to target clock period
    from_pins: Source register clock pins, must end with /C (e.g., "src_reg[*]/C")
    to_pins: Target register data pins, must end with /D (e.g., "dst_reg[*]/D")

Notes:
    - Important: from_pins must be clock pins (/C), not /Q or clock names
    - Important: to_pins must be data pins (/D), not /Q
    - Skew constraints are not affected by clock_groups/false_path/max_delay
    - Can use wildcards for multiple pins (e.g., "reg[*]/C")
    - Recommend using with set_max_delay -datapath_only for layout optimization

Examples:
    # Gray code pointer CDC skew constraint (correct example)
    set_bus_skew(2.5, from_pins="gray_rd_ptr_reg[*]/C", to_pins="gray_wr_ptr_reg[*]/D")

    # 8-bit data bus skew
    set_bus_skew(0.5, from_pins="tx_data_reg[*]/C", to_pins="rx_data_reg[*]/D")

    # Wrong examples (will produce warnings):
    # - from_pins="clk_a" -> Wrong! Use pins, not clock names
    # - from_pins="reg[*]/Q" -> Wrong! Use /C not /Q

tools.name: sim_probe

tools.description:
Sample signal values over time and return a waveform table.

        Re-runs the compiled snapshot (no re-compilation needed) and samples
        specified signals at regular intervals, returning an aligned text table.

        Use sim_list_signals() first if unsure about signal paths.

        IMPORTANT: Use time_range to set start/end time, NOT start_time/end_time.

        Args:
            signals: Comma-separated signal paths (e.g. "dut/count,dut/en,clk")
            time_range: "start:end" time window. Examples:
                "0ns:all" (default, full simulation)
                "50ns:200ns" (specific window)
                "100us:500us" (microsecond range)
                "0ns:1ms" (from start to 1ms)
            step: Sampling interval (e.g. "10ns", "1us", "500ns"). Choose based on
                time_range to stay within max_samples limit.
            max_samples: Maximum number of samples to capture (default 200, hard limit 2000).
                If time_range/step would exceed this, sampling stops early.
            radix: Display radix: hex, bin, dec (mapped to unsigned), oct
            timeout_sec: Timeout in seconds (default 300, increase for long simulations)

        Examples:

            sim_probe(signals="dut/rst_n,dut/state", time_range="0ns:1us", step="10ns")

            # Probe FSM at microsecond scale
            sim_probe(signals="ctrl/state", time_range="100us:500us", step="1us")

tools.name: sim_stop
tools.summary: Stop a stuck/background xsim simulation and clear its snapshot lock.
tools.description:
Stop a stuck/background xsim simulation and clear its snapshot lock.

        Use this when sim_compile() reports SIM_LOCKED (XSIM 43-3345 "Unable to
        remove previous simulation file xsimk.exe"). That error means a previous
        kernel launched by sim_run_async()/sim_run() is still running and is
        locking xsim.dir/mcp_snapshot/xsimk.exe, so xelab cannot rebuild the
        snapshot. On Windows a running .exe cannot be overwritten, so every
        re-compile keeps failing until the kernel is killed.

        This terminates the stale xsim kernel(s) and removes the locked snapshot
        so the next sim_compile() rebuilds cleanly. Note: it kills ALL xsim
        kernels on this machine (the standalone engine controls one sim at a
        time), so do not call it while an unrelated xsim run you care about is
        still in progress.
